born.why: The code improves safety by using trait-based inference (color, shape, smell) to assess risk for new fruits, preventing catastrophic errors when specific species history is scarce or ambiguous.

It prioritizes survival by checking specific historical data for the fruit's key, infers safety from shared traits (smell/color) when history is missing, and only eats when safe evidence exists or starvation is critical, preventing death from poisonous fruits.

The code improves safety by strictly avoiding known poisonous fruits unless starving, prioritizes eating known-safe fruits when hungry, and uses tasting to gather data on new fruits only when hunger justifies the risk, ensuring Fagi lives longer by minimizing poison consumption while maximizing food intake.

The previous code treated all past experiences equally and didn't distinguish between "unknown" and "uncertain". This rewrite uses recency-weighted safety scoring for each species. It avoids toxic fruits more aggressively (threshold -2), allows tasting unknown fruits only if hunger is moderate (to minimize starvation risk while gathering info), and prioritizes eating known-safe fruits when hungry, thereby reducing unnecessary starvation and poisoning risks.

The code prioritizes avoiding known poisonous fruits by checking the diary for past harm to the same key, and uses a hunger-threshold strategy to choose between eating immediately, carrying for later, or tasting new/known safe fruits.

The code prioritizes survival by eating unknown food only when starving (>90 hunger), avoids known poisonous fruits unless desperate, and aggressively eats proven safe fruits to build energy reserves, while avoiding unnecessary risks on new fruits unless hunger justifies the trial.

The code improves safety by using smell and key traits to generalize poison knowledge across species (e.g., if one "sharp" fruit is toxic, others might be too), prioritizes eating only when high-confidence safe or critically starving, and avoids tasting ambiguous fruits unless hunger is manageable.
